data.title: Nightclub and DJ Booth
data.summary: Realistic nightclub models: a DJ booth with decks, mixer and players, riser and facade modules, LED video and dance floor tiles, speaker stacks, truss, moving heads and a mirror ball, a modular bar with its back bar and glassware, booths, and the entrance and cloakroom kit.
data.description: A modern realistic nightclub library for building a whole club: the room, the booth, the show and the bar. Nine modular systems make the place itself: a 2 m club floor tile, a 1 m LED dance floor tile in three colours, a 1 m backdrop video panel that tiles across and up, a 2 by 1 m riser, a 1.5 m booth facade run, 300 mm box truss in 2 m bays with corner and four way junction blocks, a 1.5 m bar counter run with a square corner, a 1.2 by 2.6 m wall module that takes either a mirror panel or the entrance door, and an acoustic panel run. The booth is modelled as a booth: a laminate desk on steel cheeks carrying two turntables with real platters, tonearms and headshells, two media players with dished jog wheels, a four channel mixer, a laptop on its stand, headphones and a crate of records. Sound is a sub and a trapezoidal top box that stack or fly in a bumper frame; light is a moving head whose tilting head is parented to its panning yoke, strobe and UV bars, a housed laser, a mirror ball on its rotator, par bars on stands and a smoke machine. The bar has a panelled counter with a brass foot rail and stone top, a lit back bar stocked with twenty eight bottles, an optics rail, a four tap font, a glass washer, an ice well with its speed rail, a cocktail station, stools, a till and an overhead stemware rack. Around them: raised velvet booths with tables, rope and belt barriers, a cloakroom, a door host podium, signage, vents, bins and a cleaning trolley. Every model carries real material contrast, so it reads under plain light and not only under club lighting. The entrance leaf, the glass washer hood, the cocktail drawer, the moving head yoke and head, the turntable platters, the mirror ball and the trolley wheels are named nodes on their own pivots with rigid open, close, spin, tilt and roll clips: node transforms only, no skinning. Cables, light beams, laser fans, smoke, the barrier rope and belt, hanging garments and speaker cones stay static, because a flexible run, a beam or a moving cone is not reachable with a rigid node transform and faking it costs a consumer more than it gives. Every file is self contained CC0 geometry with no collision or navigation data.

starterScene.summary: A whole small club laid out from the pack's own kit on its own floor: a 12 by 10 m room of 2 m club floor tiles with a 4 m LED dance floor chequered into the middle of it. At one end the DJ booth stands on three riser modules behind a run of facade panels, with the decks,...
starterScene.description: A whole small club laid out from the pack's own kit on its own floor: a 12 by 10 m room of 2 m club floor tiles with a 4 m LED dance floor chequered into the middle of it. At one end the DJ booth stands on three riser modules behind a run of facade panels, with the decks, mixer, players, laptop and headphones laid out on the desk, monitor wedges and record crates beside it, a ten panel video wall across the back and a speaker stack each side carrying a laser and a strobe. A six metre truss ring flies overhead on corner and junction blocks, with delay speakers hung under it and the mirror ball turning in the middle. Down one side, a bar run of counter modules with a corner, the back bar stocked with bottles, taps, a till, the wash and cocktail kit behind it, stools in front and the stemware rack overhead. Down the other, three raised booths with their tables. At the back, the entrance wall with its door module, the cloakroom, the rope and belt barriers and the door host podium, with the signage, vents, bins and the cleaning trolley that finish a room off.
